Nora (PM): Quick thread: we need a fresh RICE pass for q next. Current top 5 are monopolized by two large customer asks. Thinking we should: 1) split big epics into deliverable slices, 2) penalize sequence-cost for blockers, and 3) reweight impact to reflect breadth not just $ of one pilot. Thoughts?
Eli (SWE): +1. Engineering prefers smaller verticals we can land incrementally. Example: split 'enterprise-keying' -> "KMS adapter" (1w) + "audit export" (3w) + "full rotation" (4w). That surfaces value earlier.
Ravi (Infra): From infra view, some infra work (batching + prefix cache) has high operational ROI but low direct revenue signal. If we upweight ops-savings in impact calculation, these jump up. Also note staging windows: some infra changes require DB migration windows, that adds hidden effort.
Tess (Data): I ran a quick sensitivity model. If impact = 0.6*reach + 0.3*revenue + 0.1*strategic, predictive-cache moves from rank 12 -> 4. I can paste the sheet. Here's the normalizer I used (pseudo):
```
# per-customer effect -> median-normalized
norm_impact = median_effect / median(median_effects)
weighted_impact = 0.6*reach + 0.3*revenue + 0.1*strategic
rice = (reach * weighted_impact * confidence) / effort
```
Hana (Sales): From a conversion angle, customers care about early proofs. If we can deliver the KMS adapter in 1 sprint, several pilots can sign POs faster. So decomposing helps pipeline.
Nora (PM): Proposal: we do a two-pass: 1) "decomposed RICE" where large epics are split into sub-epics and rescored; 2) add a new column "sequence_cost" = number_of_dependents * 0.5 (penalty) and subtract from score; 3) produce top-20 with old vs new rank deltas. Can team deliver numbers by EOD?
Eli (SWE): I'll re-estimate effort for top 15 and flag migrations.
Ravi (Infra): I'll annotate any items requiring canary+db-migrate windows and estimate sequence_cost impact.
Tess (Data): I'll output a CSV with old_score,new_score,rank_delta and a tiny chart. Expect by 3:30p.
Hana (Sales): I'll prioritize customer asks to map which decomposed slices unblock >1 deal.
Nora (PM): If the outcome is that infra work rises, can we still protect a ship lane for product bets? We should avoid a single resource-sink.
Eli (SWE): Agree. Suggest we create a "platform runway" bucket with fixed capacity and cap how many infra tickets can move into the quarter unless they have >x ROI.
Nora (PM): Ok — owners: Eli (effort), Ravi (deps & seq cost), Tess (recalc + visuals), Hana (sales mapping). Reconvene 16:30 to triage top 20 and lock quarter. Thanks. :rocket:
deploy-bot: Canary for "predictive-cache" at 5% in eu-west-1.
